title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 2
paragraphs: Thus spoke Artaphrenes regarding the revolt; and Histiaeus, fearing Artaphrenes because he understood the matter, ran away the next night at nightfall and went to the coast, having deceived King Darius—seeing that he had undertaken to subdue Sardinia, the largest of islands, and was instead trying to assume leadership of the Ionians in the war against Darius. Then crossing over to Chios, he was put in bonds by the Chians, who accused him of working for a change in their government on Darius's instructions. When, however, the Chians learned the whole story and heard that he was an enemy of the king, they released him.
